title: I Fell for This Crypto Ad (So You Don't Have To)
creator: Owen Gallagher
description:
A crypto trading app ad kept showing up in my feed, so I signed up with a burner account to see where it went. Spoiler: nowhere good.

If you've lost money to a scam like this, report it to your bank straight away and to Action Fraud.

I'm not linking the app or the site for obvious reasons.

sentences.t: For about three weeks, the same ad kept showing up every time I opened my phone.
A guy on a yacht, telling me he turned five hundred quid into a house.
And eventually I thought, right, I'm going to see exactly where this goes.
So first, I want you to hear the actual pitch, because it's really well written, and that's the scary part.
I wrote it down word for word.
Are you tired of working nine to five while other people get rich?
QuantumTrade Pro uses artificial intelligence to trade crypto for you, twenty four hours a day, with a ninety-four percent success rate.
Sign up today, use code MOON50, and get fifty percent off your first deposit fee, but only for the next hundred people.
Head to the link in the description before this offer disappears forever.
That's it, that's the whole ad, and every single sentence in it is a red flag.
Let's break it down.
Ninety-four percent success rate.
No real trading system on earth has a ninety-four percent success rate, and if it did, they would not be selling it to you on social media.
They'd be quietly using it themselves.
Then the countdown, only the next hundred people.
That's there to stop you thinking, because if you stop and think for ten minutes, you won't sign up.
And the code is a nice touch, because it makes it feel like a normal ad you'd see on any channel.
So I made a burner email and signed up.
The website looked really professional, honestly better than my actual bank.
There were testimonials from smiling people, which I reverse image searched, and they were all stock photos.
One of them was the same woman on three different scam sites under three different names.
Within about ten minutes, my phone rang.
A very friendly guy called James said he'd be my personal account manager.
He told me the minimum deposit was two hundred and fifty pounds, and that he'd help me make my first trades.
I said I'd think about it, and he called me back four more times that day.
Here's how this scam actually works, from what I found.
You deposit your two fifty, and the dashboard shows you making money, loads of it, really fast.
So you deposit more.
And then when you try to take money out, suddenly there's a withdrawal fee, or a tax, or a verification charge.
You pay that, and there's another one.
The numbers on the screen were never real, it's just a website showing whatever they want it to show.
So how do you protect yourself?
If an ad promises guaranteed returns, it's a scam, full stop.
If someone calls you to be your account manager after you sign up for an app, hang up.
If they ask you to install remote access software on your computer, absolutely hang up.
And if you've already sent money, call your bank right now, today, because the faster you report it, the better your chances.
I reported the ad to the platform, by the way, three times.
It's still running.
So please share this with anyone in your life who might fall for something like this, especially parents and grandparents.
I'll see you next week.
